title: Expressive limits: well-ordering and finite reachability
summary: Use compactness to show that well-ordering and connectedness cannot be first-order axiomatized, and finite reachability has no uniform first-order definition.
abstract: Every nonempty part of a well-ordered set has a first element. Two points are connected by a relation when a finite sequence of steps joins them. Both requirements are easy to state in ordinary mathematics, but first-order logic cannot describe them uniformly. The obstruction is visible in finite tests: a well-order can contain an arbitrarily long finite descending sequence, and two points in a connected chain can be arbitrarily far apart. Compactness turns these finite possibilities into structures that defeat any proposed first-order description. We give the actual finite witnesses, distinguish a fixed path length from an arbitrary finite length, and explain why allowing infinitely many first-order axioms does not solve the problem.

based_on.title: Lecture Notes: An Introduction to Model Theory
